Title: Computational Unified Graph Hierarchy Model
Assignee_Authors: o9 Solutions, Inc. (S. Verma et al.)
Problem_Addressed: Hierarchical and non-hierarchical link modeling across multidimensional enterprise planning measures.
Input_Data: Multidimensional relational enterprise database records and planning measures.
Prediction_Mechanism: Rule-based and statistical aggregation over relational nodes.
Scenario_Mechanism: Measure override on graph nodes propagating through relational links.
Cross_Domain_Mechanism: Graph entity relationships connecting sales, inventory, and supply.
Financial_Impact_Mechanism: Linear roll-up through planning measure formulas.
Architecture: Enterprise Knowledge Graph (EKG) and in-memory engine.
Similarity_to_DecisionSphere: Uses graph dependencies to propagate scenario interventions across business domains.
Key_Difference: o9 models enterprise state as a unified database graph of measures; DecisionSphere couples heterogeneous, independently trained statistical ML models through a 6-tier epistemic state-space operator with Platt calibration.
Potential_Overlap: Cross-domain propagation of scenario shocks through directed relationships.
Potential_Distinguishing_Feature: Strict mathematical coupling of Platt-calibrated probabilities into non-linear step penalties; cryptographic model immutability (SHA-256 digests).

Title: Plan Modeling Visualization and Interactive Scenario Simulation
Assignee_Authors: o9 Solutions, Inc. (C. Modi et al.)
Problem_Addressed: Visualizing modeled events and determining effects across complex planning frameworks.
Input_Data: User-defined event overrides and enterprise planning matrices.
Prediction_Mechanism: Deterministic formula re-evaluation and time-series projection.
Scenario_Mechanism: Event injection creating alternative scenario branches.
Cross_Domain_Mechanism: Dependency links across demand, supply, and financial measures.
Architecture: Interactive UI coupled to EKG Digital Brain.
Technical_Implementation: Client-server visualization engine on graph store.
Similarity_to_DecisionSphere: Simulates 'what-if' events and displays waterfall impacts across operational and financial KPIs.
Key_Difference: Focuses on UI visualization of database event propagation; does not formalize post-hoc probability calibration or epistemic tier demarcation across decoupled machine learning models.
Potential_Overlap: Interactive scenario lever adjustment and waterfall visual feedback.
Potential_Distinguishing_Feature: Epistemic separation of PREDICTED statistical inferences vs CALCULATED accounting line items; lexicographic gating rule.

Title: Cognitive Network Graph for Concurrent Supply Chain Planning
Assignee_Authors: Kinaxis Inc. (B. Dent et al.)
Problem_Addressed: Latency and data desynchronization caused by sequential cascaded supply chain planning.
Input_Data: ERP transactions, purchase orders, bills of materials, shipping manifests.
Prediction_Mechanism: Linear heuristics, moving averages, and lead-time estimation.
Scenario_Mechanism: In-memory versioned delta tracking across graph nodes.
Cross_Domain_Mechanism: Concurrent planning network linking demand nodes to inventory, bills of materials, and logistics nodes.
Risk_Mechanism: Constraint-violation scoring and buffer depletion indexing.
Financial_Impact_Mechanism: Direct unit cost and penalty accumulation.
Explainability_Mechanism: Root-cause constraint tracing along supply chain network paths.
Technical_Implementation: Proprietary in-memory object engine with multi-user branching.
Similarity_to_DecisionSphere: Replaces sequential planning with concurrent propagation of demand and logistics disruptions.
Key_Difference: Kinaxis relies on a single synchronized in-memory supply chain graph; DecisionSphere couples distinct, heterogeneous ML models (XGBoost) trained on disconnected open benchmarks and evaluates cross-domain human-capital strain (overtime burnout).
Potential_Overlap: Propagation of demand changes directly into logistics delay risks.
Potential_Distinguishing_Feature: Inclusion of human workforce attrition dynamics conditioned on logistics strain; Platt-calibrated expected loss modeling.

Title: Creating Data in a Data Store Using a Dynamic Ontology and Scenario Simulation
Assignee_Authors: Palantir Technologies Inc. (A. Karp et al.)
Problem_Addressed: Integrating heterogeneous operational data into dynamic object ontologies for simulation and sandboxing.
Input_Data: Unstructured, tabular, and geospatial enterprise data feeds.
Prediction_Mechanism: Configurable rule functions and plug-in statistical estimators.
Scenario_Mechanism: Sandboxed ontology forks with auto-rebasing against production.
Risk_Mechanism: Rule-based risk triggers on object attributes.
Explainability_Mechanism: Ontology lineage and object audit trails.
Similarity_to_DecisionSphere: Isolates scenario simulations from baseline production data to prevent mutation; links cross-domain entities.
Key_Difference: Palantir provides a general-purpose semantic data integration platform requiring manual ontology modeling; DecisionSphere provides a self-contained, domain-specific 13-stage deterministic execution pipeline linking trained ML models.
Potential_Overlap: Sandboxed scenario evaluation without baseline data mutation.
Potential_Distinguishing_Feature: Cryptographic runtime model hashing (SHA-256); automated probability calibration and margin collapse tipping-point discovery.

Title: System and Method for Synchronized Demand and Supply Planning
Assignee_Authors: JDA Software Group, Inc. (now Blue Yonder)
Problem_Addressed: Synchronizing promotional demand forecasts with warehouse replenishment schedules.
Input_Data: Point-of-sale (POS) data, promotional calendars, inventory records.
Prediction_Mechanism: Statistical time-series forecasting (ARIMA, Holt-Winters).
Cross_Domain_Mechanism: Demand forecast ingested as direct independent input to MRP/DRP tables.
Risk_Mechanism: Stockout probability based on safety stock distribution.
Financial_Impact_Mechanism: Gross margin and inventory holding cost formulas.
Technical_Implementation: C++ / SQL relational enterprise planning package.
Similarity_to_DecisionSphere: Evaluates the impact of promotional campaigns on supply chain inventory and logistics.
Key_Difference: Uses static linear statistical models and MRP schedules; does not model workforce attrition, non-linear machine learning classifiers, or probability calibration.
Potential_Overlap: Promotional demand shock propagation into logistics fulfillment.
Potential_Distinguishing_Feature: Multi-tier epistemic hierarchy preventing causal hallucination; gradient boosted decision trees with TreeSHAP attributions.

Title: Integrated Business Planning and Scenario Comparison
Assignee_Authors: SAP SE (M. Becker et al.)
Problem_Addressed: Real-time scenario simulation and financial comparison across sales, operations, and supply chain.
Input_Data: SAP HANA in-memory ERP tables (sales orders, inventory, capacity).
Prediction_Mechanism: Statistical demand sensing and linear optimization.
Scenario_Mechanism: HANA versioned scenario copies with parameter delta overlays.
Cross_Domain_Mechanism: Shared columnar database tables with cross-module joins.
Risk_Mechanism: Capacity utilization thresholds and SLA breach flags.
Architecture: SAP S/4HANA & SAP IBP cloud architecture.
Similarity_to_DecisionSphere: Computes net profit deltas and compares scenario alternatives against baseline operations.
Key_Difference: Tightly coupled to proprietary ERP transactional schemas; relies on classical operations research / linear programming rather than decoupled probabilistic ML models with calibration error bounds.
Potential_Overlap: Scenario delta comparison against historical enterprise baseline.
Potential_Distinguishing_Feature: Model-agnostic decoupling of ML models via explicit mathematical state vectors; lexicographic risk gating.

Title: Cognitive Decision Support System for Multi-Domain Risk Evaluation
Assignee_Authors: International Business Machines Corp. (IBM)
Problem_Addressed: Synthesizing multi-source unstructured and structured data to evaluate operational risk.
Input_Data: Text documents, sensor streams, operational logs.
Prediction_Mechanism: Natural language processing and Bayesian risk scoring.
Scenario_Mechanism: Hypothetical event injection into Bayesian belief network.
Cross_Domain_Mechanism: Conditional probability tables in directed graphical model.
Technical_Implementation: Java / REST service with graphical model inference.
Similarity_to_DecisionSphere: Evaluates risk across multiple domains using probabilistic scoring and evidence paths.
Key_Difference: Relies on subjective Bayesian prior elicitations and NLP Watson services; DecisionSphere combines empirical tree ensembles on tabular data with rigorous Platt calibration and deterministic cost accounting.
Potential_Overlap: Probabilistic risk propagation across multi-domain operational nodes.
Potential_Distinguishing_Feature: Deterministic 13-stage accounting engine avoiding generative or subjective hallucinations; TreeSHAP feature attributions.

Title: Cascading Failure Modeling and Risk Propagation Across Interconnected Systems
Assignee_Authors: International Business Machines Corp. (IBM)
Problem_Addressed: Simulating cascading failure propagation across interdependent physical and logistical networks.
Input_Data: Network topology graphs, failure probability distributions.
Prediction_Mechanism: Epidemic spreading models / percolation theory.
Cross_Domain_Mechanism: Inter-network dependency edges with transmission probabilities.
Risk_Mechanism: Fraction of collapsed nodes / systemic collapse index.
Similarity_to_DecisionSphere: Simulates cascading failure/risk propagation across connected operational domains.
Key_Difference: Focuses on topological network percolation (power grids, telecommunications); does not evaluate enterprise commercial levers, machine learning regression/classification on tabular data, or managerial accounting.
Potential_Overlap: Cross-domain propagation of localized disruptions into systemic strain.
Potential_Distinguishing_Feature: Enterprise-specific coupling parameters (ASM-001 to ASM-008) linking retail demand shocks to logistics delays and human burnout.

Title: Multi-Dimensional In-Memory Calculation Engine for Scenario Modeling
Assignee_Authors: Anaplan, Inc. (M. Gould)
Problem_Addressed: Performance bottlenecks in recalculating large multi-dimensional business planning models during what-if analysis.
Input_Data: Multi-dimensional hypercubes (dimensions: Time, Product, Org, Line Item).
Prediction_Mechanism: User-defined spreadsheet formulas (non-ML).
Scenario_Mechanism: Cell value override with selective dependency recalculation.
Explainability_Mechanism: Formula audit trail / cell dependency tree.
Similarity_to_DecisionSphere: Enables rapid what-if scenario modeling and calculates financial bottom-line impacts.
Key_Difference: Anaplan is a deterministic spreadsheet calculation engine that contains no statistical machine learning, no probability calibration, no explainability, and no automated risk gating.
Potential_Overlap: Fast recalculation of downstream financial statements from parameter inputs.
Potential_Distinguishing_Feature: Integration of calibrated gradient boosted decision trees for operational risk estimation; lexicographic decision gating.

Title: Method and System for Automated Decision Intelligence and Strategy Optimization
Assignee_Authors: Quantellia LLC (M. Pratt et al.)
Problem_Addressed: Bridging machine learning predictions to actionable business outcomes without unintended consequences.
Input_Data: Operational metrics, ML model outputs, decision constraints.
Prediction_Mechanism: External predictive model ingestion.
Scenario_Mechanism: Decision lever adjustment in causal decision diagrams.
Cross_Domain_Mechanism: Causal Decision Diagrams (CDDs) linking levers, intermediate states, and outcomes.
Risk_Mechanism: Constraint satisfaction and risk metric roll-up.
Similarity_to_DecisionSphere: Shares the core Decision Intelligence paradigm of mapping actions through predictions to business outcomes.
Key_Difference: Quantellia asserts causal relationships in CDDs without strict non-causal epistemic demarcation; does not implement Platt probability calibration, cryptographic runtime model verification, or specific operational-financial coupling parameters.
Potential_Overlap: Conceptual workflow: Decision Levers -> Predictive Inferences -> Business Impact -> Recommendations.
Potential_Distinguishing_Feature: Strict 6-tier epistemic hierarchy preventing causal overreach (Shmueli 2010); bounded calibration error propagation.

Title: Decision Intelligence: Augmenting Human Decisions with Machine Learning
Assignee_Authors: Pratt, L., & Cane, M. (IEEE Computer / Gartner)
Problem_Addressed: High failure rate of enterprise AI projects due to isolation of ML predictions from actual business decisions.
Input_Data: Conceptual decision models and heterogeneous enterprise data.
Prediction_Mechanism: Black-box ML models.
Technical_Implementation: High-level architectural methodology (no concrete code implementation).
Similarity_to_DecisionSphere: Foundational conceptual framework describing cross-domain decision support.
Key_Difference: High-level conceptual methodology without formal mathematical operators, concrete code implementations, probability calibration, or auditable benchmarks.
Potential_Overlap: The overarching goal of connecting predictive models to decision trade-offs.
Potential_Distinguishing_Feature: Concrete, deterministic 13-stage algorithmic architecture with empirical benchmarking and cryptographic integrity.

Title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
Assignee_Authors: Guo, C., Pleiss, G., Sun, Y., & Weinberger, K. Q. (ICML 2017)
Problem_Addressed: Modern deep neural networks are miscalibrated (overconfident), producing unreliable probability estimates.
Input_Data: Validation set logits and ground truth labels.
Prediction_Mechanism: Temperature scaling, vector scaling, Platt scaling, isotonic regression.
Risk_Mechanism: Expected Calibration Error (ECE) and Brier Score evaluation.
Similarity_to_DecisionSphere: Utilizes post-hoc calibration metrics (ECE, Brier score) to evaluate probability reliability.
Key_Difference: Evaluates calibration purely within isolated neural networks; DecisionSphere proves the operational and financial consequence of calibration when probabilities are multiplied by contractual dollar penalties in downstream operations.
Potential_Overlap: Platt Sigmoid scaling formulation and ECE measurement.
Potential_Distinguishing_Feature: Integration of calibrated probabilities into downstream non-linear step penalties, preventing massive financial miscalculation ($38k error).

Title: Probabilistic Outputs for Support Vector Machines and Comparisons to Regularized Likelihood Methods
Assignee_Authors: Platt, J. (Advances in Large Margin Classifiers)
Problem_Addressed: Transforming uncalibrated classification margin distances into calibrated posterior probabilities.
Input_Data: Classifier output margins and binary targets.
Prediction_Mechanism: Parametric logistic sigmoid fitting: P(Y=1|z) = 1 / (1 + exp(A*z + B)).
Similarity_to_DecisionSphere: Identical mathematical calibration equation used in DecisionSphere's supply chain and workforce classifiers.
Key_Difference: Platt scaling is an unpatentable foundational mathematical technique (Grade A: Known Technique). DecisionSphere claims only its specific architectural integration into downstream operational coupling.
Potential_Overlap: Mathematical formula for Sigmoid probability calibration.
Potential_Distinguishing_Feature: Coupling calibrated probabilities to contractual delay penalties and turnover replacement costs.

Title: A Unified Approach to Interpreting Model Predictions (TreeSHAP)
Assignee_Authors: Lundberg, S. M., & Lee, S.-I. (NeurIPS 2017)
Problem_Addressed: Computing exact, locally accurate Shapley feature attributions for complex tree ensembles in polynomial time.
Input_Data: Trained decision tree ensembles and feature vectors.
Prediction_Mechanism: TreeSHAP algorithm calculating marginal conditional expectations.
Risk_Mechanism: Feature attribution vectors summing to base-rate delta.
Explainability_Mechanism: Additive Shapley values in log-odds or probability space.
Similarity_to_DecisionSphere: DecisionSphere uses TreeSHAP to attribute operational risks to feature levers.
Key_Difference: TreeSHAP is an established, unpatentable XAI algorithm. DecisionSphere adopts it with strict non-causal epistemic caveats (forbidding claims of physical causation).
Potential_Overlap: Calculation of Shapley feature attributions on XGBoost models.
Potential_Distinguishing_Feature: Demarcation of SHAP attributions as Tier 2 statistical associations within an end-to-end multi-domain decision pipeline.

Title: The Ripple Effect in Supply Chains: Trade-Off Between Resilience and Efficiency
Assignee_Authors: Ivanov, D., Sokolov, B., & Dolgui, A. (IJPR)
Problem_Addressed: Analyzing how localized disruptions propagate downstream through supply network structures.
Input_Data: Supply chain node capacities, lead times, disruption parameters.
Prediction_Mechanism: Optimal control theory and discrete-event simulation (AnyLogic).
Cross_Domain_Mechanism: Multi-echelon inventory and production flow dependencies.
Risk_Mechanism: Service level degradation and lost sales ratios.
Similarity_to_DecisionSphere: Investigates the propagation of operational friction and bottlenecks across supply chains.
Key_Difference: Focuses on discrete-event supply chain dynamics; does not integrate supervised machine learning models, probability calibration, workforce attrition classifiers, or commercial promotional shocks.
Potential_Overlap: Modeling cascading downstream impact of operational delays.
Potential_Distinguishing_Feature: Coupling retail marketing campaigns to logistics bottlenecks and workforce burnout via calibrated tree models.

Title: To Explain or to Predict?
Assignee_Authors: Shmueli, G. (Statistical Science)
Problem_Addressed: Conflation between explanatory statistical modeling (causal inference) and empirical predictive modeling.
Input_Data: Observational data matrices.
Prediction_Mechanism: Statistical and algorithmic predictive models.
Similarity_to_DecisionSphere: DecisionSphere's 6-Tier Epistemic Hierarchy directly builds on Shmueli's distinction between P(Y|X) and causal mechanisms.
Key_Difference: Shmueli provides the philosophical and statistical foundation; DecisionSphere embeds this foundation into a computer-implemented decision support platform.
Potential_Overlap: Epistemic distinction between empirical correlation and causal intervention.
Potential_Distinguishing_Feature: Algorithmic enforcement of epistemic tiers in Pydantic data contracts and API responses.

Title: Why Do Tree-Based Models Still Outperform Deep Learning on Typical Tabular Data?
Assignee_Authors: Grinsztajn, L., Oyallon, E., & Varoquaux, G. (NeurIPS 2022)
Problem_Addressed: Empirical comparison of tree ensembles (XGBoost, Random Forest) vs deep architectures on tabular benchmarks.
Input_Data: 45 standardized tabular datasets.
Prediction_Mechanism: Gradient boosted trees, ResNet, FT-Transformer, Saint.
Similarity_to_DecisionSphere: Validates DecisionSphere's architectural choice of XGBoost over Deep Neural Networks for enterprise tabular data.
Key_Difference: Pure empirical machine learning benchmark; no scenario engine, cross-domain propagation, or decision-support capability.
Potential_Overlap: Demonstration that XGBoost is superior for tabular enterprise prediction.
Potential_Distinguishing_Feature: Enterprise simulation architecture built on top of validated tabular tree models.

Title: A Robust Optimization Approach to Supply Chain Management
Assignee_Authors: Bertsimas, D., & Thiele, A. (Operations Research)
Problem_Addressed: Inventory and supply chain control under demand uncertainty using robust optimization without known probability distributions.
Input_Data: Demand uncertainty sets, holding costs, backorder penalties.
Prediction_Mechanism: Polyhedral uncertainty sets.
Financial_Impact_Mechanism: Linear cost minimization under worst-case realization.
Similarity_to_DecisionSphere: Evaluates operational and financial performance under uncertain demand and capacity constraints.
Key_Difference: Uses static linear programming solvers for worst-case optimization; does not utilize trained machine learning models, empirical holdout datasets, or human attrition dynamics.
Potential_Overlap: Formulation of inventory and penalty cost accounting.
Potential_Distinguishing_Feature: Empirical ML prediction conditioned on complex tabular features coupled with deterministic managerial accounting.

Title: Method and Apparatus for Workforce and Capacity Planning in a Service Organization
Assignee_Authors: Accenture Global Services GmbH (S. Bagchi et al.)
Problem_Addressed: Optimizing workforce allocation and overtime scheduling against incoming demand volume in service organizations.
Input_Data: Project demand forecasts, employee skills, labor costs.
Prediction_Mechanism: Linear programming / queueing models.
Risk_Mechanism: SLA delay probability based on queue length.
Financial_Impact_Mechanism: Labor payroll and overtime cost calculation.
Similarity_to_DecisionSphere: Models the relationship between incoming workload and workforce overtime/capacity strain.
Key_Difference: Focuses on static queueing and shift optimization; does not model employee attrition risk via machine learning, nor does it couple workforce directly to retail sales promotions or shipping logistics.
Potential_Overlap: Calculation of overtime costs under demand surges.
Potential_Distinguishing_Feature: Coupling overtime directly to predictive attrition risk ($30k replacement cost) and logistics carrier penalties.

Title: System and Method for Supply Chain Disruption Risk Assessment Using Machine Learning
Assignee_Authors: Resilinc Corp. (B. Bindi et al.)
Problem_Addressed: Monitoring and predicting supplier disruptions using multi-source news, weather, and operational data.
Input_Data: Supplier location maps, event news feeds, historic disruption logs.
Prediction_Mechanism: NLP event classification and supplier risk scoring.
Cross_Domain_Mechanism: BOM mapping from supplier to product lines.
Architecture: SaaS supply chain mapping and event monitoring platform.
Technical_Implementation: Cloud-hosted event detection and risk aggregation engine.
Similarity_to_DecisionSphere: Assesses supply chain risk and calculates revenue at risk under operational disruptions.
Key_Difference: Resilinc monitors external supplier catastrophic events (earthquakes, factory fires); DecisionSphere models internally induced commercial disruptions (marketing campaigns causing warehouse backlogs and workforce burnout).
Potential_Overlap: Financial valuation of supply chain delivery risks.
Potential_Distinguishing_Feature: Simulating internally generated cross-domain friction across demand, shipping, and labor.

Title: Method and System for Automated Machine Learning Pipeline Execution and Governance
Assignee_Authors: DataRobot, Inc. (J. Acheson et al.)
Problem_Addressed: Automating feature engineering, model selection, calibration, and deployment for enterprise tabular datasets.
Input_Data: Raw tabular CSV/database tables.
Prediction_Mechanism: AutoML leaderboard (XGBoost, LightGBM, ElasticNet, Neural Nets).
Scenario_Mechanism: What-if feature prediction on deployed model endpoint.
Cross_Domain_Mechanism: None (models are deployed as isolated single-target endpoints).
Financial_Impact_Mechanism: User-defined payoff matrices on single classifiers.
Explainability_Mechanism: SHAP feature importances and partial dependence plots.
Similarity_to_DecisionSphere: Uses XGBoost, probability calibration, and SHAP explanations on tabular data.
Key_Difference: DataRobot is an isolated model training and deployment platform; it does not model cross-domain scenario propagation between multiple decoupled models, nor does it implement multi-stage managerial accounting.
Potential_Overlap: Model calibration and SHAP explanations for tabular classification.
Potential_Distinguishing_Feature: Multi-domain orchestration pipeline propagating outputs across heterogeneous models into a unified decision gating engine.

Title: Managing Risk to Avoid Supply-Chain Breakdown
Assignee_Authors: Chopra, S., & Sodhi, M. S. (MIT Sloan Management Review)
Problem_Addressed: Categorizing supply chain risks (disruptions, delays, forecast errors, capacity) and mitigating trade-offs.

Potential_Overlap: Identification of conflicting operational priorities in supply networks.
Potential_Distinguishing_Feature: Fully computerized, deterministic mathematical calculation of net operating profit delta and automated gating.

Title: System and Method for Cross-Enterprise Scenario Simulation in a Multi-Tenant Cloud Architecture
Assignee_Authors: Coupa Software Inc. (LLamasoft) (T. Ward et al.)
Problem_Addressed: Simulating global supply chain networks under demand volatility and tariff changes.
Input_Data: Supply chain node locations, transportation lanes, tariffs, customer demand.
Prediction_Mechanism: Mixed integer linear programming (MILP) network solvers.
Scenario_Mechanism: Network topology alteration and demand volume scaling.
Explainability_Mechanism: Geospatial flow maps and cost breakdown charts.

Similarity_to_DecisionSphere: Simulates operational scenarios and evaluates total cost impacts.
Key_Difference: Focuses on strategic physical network design (facility locations, transportation lanes); does not evaluate short-term promotional shocks, workforce overtime/burnout, or machine learning probability calibration.
Potential_Overlap: Simulation of demand volume scaling on logistics costs.
Potential_Distinguishing_Feature: Coupling short-term marketing shocks to workforce burnout and carrier penalties via calibrated tree models.

Title: Predicting Good Probabilities With Supervised Learning
Assignee_Authors: Niculescu-Mizil, A., & Caruana, R. (ICML 2005)
Problem_Addressed: Evaluating the probability calibration of diverse learning algorithms (SVM, boosted trees, neural nets).
Input_Data: Empirical supervised learning benchmarks.
Prediction_Mechanism: Platt scaling and Isotonic regression applied to model outputs.
Risk_Mechanism: Brier score and squared error measurement.
Similarity_to_DecisionSphere: Evaluates Platt scaling on boosted trees using reliability diagrams.
Key_Difference: Foundational empirical machine learning paper; no scenario propagation, no cross-domain coupling, no financial accounting.
Potential_Overlap: Comparison of Sigmoid (Platt) vs Isotonic regression for probability calibration.
Potential_Distinguishing_Feature: Downstream propagation of calibrated probabilities into contractual step penalties.

Title: System and Method for Supply Chain Exception Management and Automated Resolution
Assignee_Authors: JDA Software Group, Inc. (now Blue Yonder)
Problem_Addressed: Detecting logistics delays and triggering automated operational mitigations.
Input_Data: Shipment tracking events, order promises, carrier schedules.
Prediction_Mechanism: Estimated time of arrival (ETA) calculation.
Cross_Domain_Mechanism: Alert propagation to customer service and warehouse.
Risk_Mechanism: Late delivery flag and SLA breach severity.
Financial_Impact_Mechanism: Expedited freight fee vs penalty trade-off.
Similarity_to_DecisionSphere: Triggers strategic actions (such as switching to expedited air freight) based on delivery delay risks.
Key_Difference: Reactive post-order operational execution system; DecisionSphere is a pre-execution strategic planning simulator that evaluates hypothetical scenarios before real-world orders are placed.
Potential_Overlap: Rule-based mitigation triggers (e.g., expedited air freight surcharge ACT-SC-001).
Potential_Distinguishing_Feature: Pre-execution simulation coupling demand shock to human labor overtime and turnover costs.
